title: Device-independent Certification Of Majorana Fermions And A New Self-testing Equivalence
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 October 2026;
tldr: The paper develops device-independent methods to certify Majorana fermions and establishes a new self-testing equivalence relevant to quantum certification protocols.
motivation: Majorana fermions are promising for topological quantum computation, but their experimental certification is challenging because conventional tomographic approaches rely on trusted devices. Device-independent certification can provide strong, assumption-light verification based on quantum nonlocality.
method: The authors formulate device-independent certification protocols for Majorana fermion systems and introduce a new self-testing equivalence that connects observable correlations to the underlying Majorana mode structure.
result: They obtain self-testing statements and device-independent witnesses that can certify the presence of Majorana fermions from measured Bell-type correlations without trusting the measurement devices.
conclusion: The work extends self-testing and device-independent certification to topological quantum systems, offering a rigorous route to verify Majorana fermions and strengthening the toolbox of quantum information certification.

title: Simultaneously Achieving Heisenberg- And Landau-limited Precision In Equilibrium Quantum Thermometry
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 23 October 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes an equilibrium quantum thermometry approach that simultaneously attains Heisenberg-limited and Landau-limited precision.
motivation: High-precision temperature estimation at the quantum scale is constrained by both quantum metrological limits and thermodynamic bounds, motivating schemes that can approach these fundamental limits together.
method: The authors analyze equilibrium quantum thermometry using quantum estimation theory, likely optimizing probe states and measurements to saturate precision bounds.
result: They show that their scheme can simultaneously achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling and Landau-limited precision in equilibrium thermometry.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical route toward optimal equilibrium quantum thermometry under fundamental quantum and thermodynamic constraints.

title: Programmable High-dimensional State Synthesis Through A 20-m Multimode Fiber Via Long-coherence Atomic Photons
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 18 October 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates programmable synthesis and transmission of high-dimensional quantum states through a 20-m multimode fiber using long-coherence atomic photons.
motivation: High-dimensional quantum states can enhance information capacity and robustness in quantum communication, but transmitting them through multimode fiber is challenging due to mode mixing and decoherence.
method: Long-coherence photons generated from an atomic source are used together with programmable mode control to synthesize high-dimensional states through a 20-m multimode fiber.
result: The authors experimentally realize programmable high-dimensional state synthesis and fiber transmission, showing that atomic photons preserve useful coherence over the multimode channel.
conclusion: This platform provides a route toward high-dimensional quantum state distribution over fiber, with potential applications in quantum network architectures.

title: Scalability Bottlenecks In Entanglement-based Satellite Quantum Key Distribution: Downlink Asymmetry, Orbit Dependence And Finite-key Effects
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 October 2026;
tldr: The paper analyzes scalability bottlenecks in entanglement-based satellite quantum key distribution, focusing on downlink asymmetry, orbital dependence, and finite-key effects.
motivation: Satellite-based entanglement distribution is a promising route to global quantum communication, but practical deployment is limited by link asymmetry, varying satellite orbits, and finite-key constraints.
method: The authors likely model entanglement-based satellite QKD links and evaluate key-rate performance under different orbital configurations and finite-key regimes, identifying dominant scalability limitations.
result: The study characterizes how downlink asymmetry and orbit-dependent loss affect achievable secret-key rates, showing that finite-key effects impose additional constraints on realistic satellite QKD operation.
conclusion: The findings highlight key engineering and protocol-level bottlenecks that must be addressed for scalable entanglement-based satellite QKD networks.

title: Genuine Continuous Quantumness
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 14 October 2026;
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes the concept of genuine continuous quantumness for continuous-variable quantum systems.
motivation: Distinguishing genuinely quantum continuous-variable behavior from classical or effectively discrete descriptions is important for foundational and resource-theoretic treatments of continuous-variable quantum information.
method: It develops a framework for characterizing continuous quantumness, likely using resource-theoretic or nonclassicality-based criteria, and applies it to continuous-variable quantum states.
result: The work provides a characterization or operational criterion for genuine continuous quantumness, clarifying which continuous-variable states possess this property.
conclusion: The paper advances the quantification and classification of quantumness in continuous-variable settings, with relevance to quantum information resource theories and quantum optics.

title: High-fidelity Flopping-mode Single-spin Operation Via Triple-dot Orbital-band Engineering
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 October 2026;
tldr: The paper demonstrates high-fidelity flopping-mode single-spin operation in a triple quantum dot by engineering orbital bands.
motivation: High-fidelity single-spin control is essential for scalable semiconductor spin-qubit processors, and flopping-mode operation offers a promising route to fast, robust electrical control.
method: The authors use a triple-dot device with orbital-band engineering to implement flopping-mode single-spin manipulation and evaluate its operational fidelity.
result: The approach achieves high-fidelity single-spin operation via triple-dot orbital-band engineering, indicating improved control performance for spin qubits.
conclusion: Triple-dot orbital-band engineering provides a viable platform for high-fidelity flopping-mode spin control relevant to semiconductor quantum-dot quantum computing.

title: Structural Control Of Two-level Defect Density Revealed By High-throughput Correlative Measurements Of Josephson Junctions
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 14 October 2026;
tldr: This paper uses high-throughput correlative measurements to link the structural properties of Josephson junctions to two-level defect density in superconducting qubit platforms.
motivation: Two-level system defects in Josephson junctions are a major source of decoherence in superconducting quantum circuits, so understanding and controlling their structural origins is important for improving qubit performance.
method: The authors perform high-throughput correlative measurements on Josephson junctions to correlate fabrication-induced structural features with the density of two-level defects.
result: The measurements reveal structural control over two-level defect density, identifying junction characteristics that can be tuned to reduce parasitic TLS losses.
conclusion: The work provides practical guidance for fabricating low-loss Josephson junctions and improving coherence in superconducting quantum hardware.

title: Quantum State Smoothing For Tracking Optical Quantum Dynamics And Recovering Purity And Squeezing
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 21 October 2026;
tldr: The paper applies quantum state smoothing to track continuous-variable optical quantum dynamics and recover purity and squeezing from measurement records.
motivation: Continuous measurement and decoherence make real-time tracking of nonclassical optical states difficult, motivating better state-estimation methods for monitoring purity and squeezing.
method: It develops and applies quantum state smoothing, which estimates a quantum state using both past and future measurement outcomes, to optical quantum dynamics.
result: Smoothing is reported to track the optical dynamics and recover purity and squeezing, improving on filtering-only state estimates.
conclusion: Quantum state smoothing provides a useful quantum-optics estimation tool for monitoring nonclassical dynamics, but it is not closely aligned with the researcher's core information-theoretic priorities.
